scope.goal: Serve TCP targets over masque CONNECT-IP by terminating TCP in userspace, keeping the T18 UDP/IP path and the RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset working.

scope.approach: in-tree minimal TCP client (not the T6/T7 device stack, which is not available in this workspace): the choice keeps the kernel dependency-free and lets the iOS extension link it. The pinned adapter's mipstack/gVisor is the reference for behaviour, not code.

wireBehaviour.handshake: active open only: SYN (MSS option = tunnel MTU - 40/60 bytes, clamped to 64..65495), SYN-ACK verification (ACK flag, ack == ISS + 1, MSS clamp), final ACK; a SYN-ACK for another sequence number or a RST fails the dial
wireBehaviour.data: one segment per transmission, bounded by peer MSS and the peer's advertised window; cumulative ACKs, PSH on data, delayed ACKs are not used (every in-order segment is acknowledged immediately)
wireBehaviour.receive: in-order delivery to the application; out-of-order segments (bounded to 32 segments / 64 KiB) are held and delivered when the gap fills; old retransmitted bytes are acknowledged again and not re-delivered; the advertised window is 65535 minus buffered bytes
wireBehaviour.retransmission: RFC 6298-style fixed 1 s initial RTO with exponential backoff to 8 s, at most 8 retries, go-back-N on the oldest unacked segment, fast retransmit after three duplicate ACKs; a zero window waits for the peer's update (no persist timer; the dial/relay timeout bounds it)
wireBehaviour.close: app half-close sends FIN after queued data; the peer's FIN ends the read side (EOF to the application) while writes may continue; both directions closed -> Closed; RST fails the stream with ConnectionReset; a final ACK for the peer's FIN is still sent after the state machine closes
wireBehaviour.mtu: the configured `mtu` (pinned default 1280) bounds the MSS and every built packet; a packet larger than the QUIC datagram limit is a named TooLarge error
wireBehaviour.targets: one tunnel and one TCP connection per `dial` (no pooling, like the other QUIC families); the target is a literal, resolved locally or, with `remote-dns-resolve`, by an A/AAAA query sent as a UDP packet through the tunnel
wireBehaviour.coexistence: CONNECT-UDP (RFC 9298) carries UDP only, so a TCP dial through it is refused by name; CONNECT-IP UDP (T18) is unchanged and still passes its 8 cases

limits: send buffer 64 KiB (queued + unacked payload); one accepted application write is clamped to 32 KiB
receive buffer 64 KiB in-order + out-of-order; 32 out-of-order segments at most
no window scaling (RFC 7323), SACK or timestamps; no urgent data; no passive open or simultaneous open
one connection per tunnel; a second concurrent TCP target on the same `masque` outbound opens a second tunnel
RTO is fixed at 1 s initially (no RTT estimation) and retransmission is go-back-N, so a lossy path is slower than the pinned stack
a peer that advertises a zero window is waited on until the dial/relay timeout (no persist probe)
one tunnel and one TCP connection per `dial` (no pooling): a WARP configuration with many TCP targets opens many QUIC/HTTP3 associations, which T7 must cap

memory.budget: T7 verifies 40,000,000 bytes (decimal) for the whole iOS VPN extension (R3)
components: QUIC connection (T10 windows): stream receive 512 KiB + connection receive 2 MiB + send 2 MiB = 4,718,592 B
QUIC datagram receive 64 KiB + send 64 KiB = 131,072 B
HTTP/3 request stream buffers (2 KiB frame + 3 KiB capsules) and control streams: ~10 KB
TCP send buffer + retained unacked payload: up to 128 KiB
TCP receive buffer (in-order + out-of-order): up to 64 KiB
command/read channels: 4 x 32 KiB writes + read chunks <= MSS: up to ~140 KiB
memory.note: ~5.24 MB decimal per concurrent TCP dial, dominated by T10's QUIC windows (as with the ~5.14 MB UDP association). The engine opens one tunnel per TCP dial and one per SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE, so T7 must cap concurrent masque sessions (or lower Limits.max_sessions); dropping the stream closes the tunnel after the pending FIN/ACK or the relay's half-close timeout.
memory.notMeasured: analytic bounds only: no device RSS was taken on an iPhone

notImplemented: TCP through the RFC 9298 CONNECT-UDP subset (the protocol carries UDP only)
passive open, simultaneous open, TCP urgent data
RTT-estimated RTO, congestion control (a fixed window/backoff scheme is used), persist timer on a zero window
TCP over IPv4 options / IPv6 extension headers (packets carrying them are dropped, like UDP)
ICMP error reporting for TCP packets that do not fit the QUIC datagram limit (a named error instead)
decisionsForT9: masque's TCP path is now real for the WARP CONNECT-IP shape (T21); a CONNECT-UDP-only configuration still refuses TCP by name. masque stays partial because h2/h3-l4proxy, gVisor and the pinned TCP stack behaviour (window scaling, SACK, congestion control) are not reproduced.
A TCP target needs the WARP shape (`private-key`, `public-key`, `ip`/`ipv6`); a plain server + `udp: true` is UDP-only, so a mixed rule set must configure the WARP shape for TCP.
decisionsForT7: Cap concurrent masque TCP dials: each is a whole CONNECT-IP tunnel (~5.24 MB decimal analytic worst case) and one TCP connection; the extension budget is 40,000,000 bytes.

The TCP stream closes its tunnel when dropped (pending FIN/ACK or the relay's half-close timeout), so aborted sessions do not outlive the relay. No pool and no background keepalive beyond the QUIC keep-alive.
No new dependency or C library was added; the iOS extension links the same ring/rustls/quinn set.
One TCP dial = one CONNECT-IP association: the analytic worst case (~5.24 MB decimal) is charged per concurrent TCP target, not shared with the UDP association.
license: No GPL-3.0 source is vendored, linked, copied or translated. The TCP state machine is written from RFC 793/1122/6298 and the pinned adapter's observed configuration shape; no mipstack/gVisor/connect-ip-go code was read into this implementation. No third-party material was added in T21.
